findings.title: View-only group permission authorizes group creation and moves
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() calls requireManage(), which delegates to this method, so an administrator granted only read access to all groups can create new groups or move an existing group to the top level. Require the MANAGE scope here and add a negative test for creation with only VIEW.

findings.title: Group enumeration uses authorization resource types and IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() searches resources by type Groups and passes/returns their authorization resource IDs. AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates individual group resources with the group ID as their name, a separately generated resource ID, and no resource type. Consequently individual group resources are not enumerated, and the all-groups resource that is enumerated contributes an authorization ID rather than a real group ID. UsersResource uses this set to restrict user searches and counts, so group-member permissions can produce empty results despite allowing access to those users individually. Enumerate the actual groups (including the all-groups case), evaluate using group IDs, and return model group IDs.

findings.title: Group-based search restriction excludes users authorized independently
findings.body: Whenever getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns a nonempty set, searchForUser() restricts the provider query to those groups before checking individual user permissions. In V2 an administrator can have both a VIEW permission on a specific user outside those groups and VIEW_MEMBERS on a group, without global user view permission. That independently authorized user is then excluded by the provider query and never reaches canView(), even though fetching the user by ID succeeds. The same restriction is applied in BruteForceUsersResource. The search must include users authorized directly as well as users authorized through groups.
